hints: A directed cycle cannot follow edges that always go from a smaller label to a larger label.
Choose any total order of the vertices.
Direct every edge forward in that order.
analogy: Every arrow climbs a staircase, so following arrows can never return to the starting step.
algorithm: For each undirected edge (a,b), output it directed from min(a,b) to max(a,b).
correctness: Every directed edge strictly increases the vertex label. A directed path therefore strictly increases its label at each step and cannot return to its start, so no directed cycle exists.
complexity: For n vertices and m edges, O(m) time and O(1) extra space when streaming edges.
